- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.27) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.23) and forecast is trending up, dampen the upward momentum by 5–15% to prevent overcorrection.
- When recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model should not overreact to new sentiment; forecast should align with 10–15 day moving average.
- If forecast is consistently higher than true outcome over 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 2–5% per day to correct for overconfidence bias.
- For horizon > 14 days, model should not assume sentiment will persist; introduce a decay factor (e.g., 0.95 per day) to reduce sentiment-driven extrapolation.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.27), avoid long-term trend forecasts; use short-term (7–14 day) smoothing instead.
